title: Cross-Lingual Support Ticket Routing
business: Global customer support teams managing inquiries in dozens of languages.
problem: Support agents struggle to manually categorize incoming tickets written in various languages, leading to slow response times and misrouted requests.
solution: Use the paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 model to map incoming support tickets into a unified 384-dimensional dense vector space, allowing for semantic similarity matching against a library of known issue categories regardless of the original language.
steps: Install the sentence-transformers library in the production environment.
Load the paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 model using the SentenceTransformer class.
Convert incoming multilingual support tickets into dense vector embeddings.
Calculate the cosine similarity between the ticket embedding and pre-computed category embeddings to identify the best match.
Route the ticket to the appropriate language-specific support queue based on the highest similarity score.
outcome: Improved routing accuracy and reduced manual triage time by automatically grouping semantically related inquiries across different languages.
limitation: The model has a maximum sequence length of 128 tokens; longer support tickets may be truncated, potentially losing context. This can be verified by checking the token count of input text before encoding.

from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
# Load the multilingual model
model = SentenceTransformer('sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2')
# Encode ticket text into 384-dimensional vectors
embeddings = model.encode(['Ticket text here', 'Texte de ticket ici'])
